prompts.title: Tower Tumble
prompts.prompt:
Create one polished original gameplay-screen concept mockup for Literacy Guide, a child-friendly literacy game collection. Use wide landscape 16:9 composition, high-quality colorful 2.5D/3D console-game art with the visual richness and readable gameplay of SNES through PS3-era family arcade games. This must look like an actual game camera caught during play, not a promotional poster, not an icon, not a diagram or a generic educational quiz. Original environments, no copyrighted Nintendo or Minecraft characters, logos or copied assets. Shared protagonist canon: Bouncy, a cheerful little yellow lamb with curly golden fleece, long drooping ears, brown oval hooves, a red neckerchief and exposed silver coil-spring lower legs. Keep the lamb silhouette and spring legs clear. Painterly/toy-like materials, crisp silhouettes, thoughtfully placed interactive obstacles. Restrained translucent HUD, rounded friendly controls, safe generous touch controls. No clutter, no giant marketing title obscuring play. Any text specified is the only text permitted. No target word is printed anywhere in world, HUD, objects, hints or signs. Blank answer slots and individual graphemes are permitted. All choice blocks/zones equally styled; do not color-code the right answer. Child has not answered this task yet.
GAME: TOWER TUMBLE. Camera is a side-on 2.5D platform game. Show a large multi-level wooden scaffold tower winding upward around an old meadow mill. Four staggered wide walkable platforms, visible ladders connecting alternating ends, a suspended cargo pulley, little rolling padded barrels, destructible masonry sections and bounce pads. Background: layered forest hills, distant quaint rooftops, bright afternoon light. Upper ledge has a tiny trapped cart waiting for rescue. Main actor Bouncy occupies the lower-middle platform, leaping to swing a comically soft wooden mallet at a reachable brick, expressive pose, spring legs bending. Nearby loose puffs and a small brick chip show hammer impact. Bricks reachable from platforms carry just these separate lowercase graphemes: "sh", "s", "ch", "i", "a", "p", "t". Distribute them plausibly in the world and never spell a complete word in a row. Correct route cannot be inferred from color. Top-left small HUD title exactly "Tower Tumble". Top center compact cream task card shows ONLY an unlabelled little sailing ship picture, a speaker symbol, and three empty square slots. No printed word for that picture. Top-right small pause button and three rescue stars, no countdown or lives. Bottom-left translucent circular left, up and right arrows for moving/climbing. Bottom-right two generous circular touch buttons labelled only "Jump" and "Smash", plus small speaker replay control. Game geometry must be credible: platform tops traversable, every ladder rests on a platform and terminates at next ledge, no detached stairs. Let actual scenery and action fill nearly all of the frame. A rescue route needs climbing and smashing, not only choosing letters.

GAME: RALLY PALS. Third-person console tennis game, slightly elevated camera behind Bouncy at near baseline. The lamb holds a blue tennis racket and prepares a lively forehand; spring legs and red scarf clear. Show a fully readable pastel green tennis court with straight white boundary lines, physical net across center, fenced edges, crowd of SMALL abstract plush silhouettes, leafy meadow club, pennants and warm sunshine. A tiny distant rival appears on far baseline. A yellow tennis ball floats just above near court, with restrained curved motion streak. The far half of court has THREE broad translucent landing zones, SAME color/material, correctly placed on the ground within the court, labels exactly "ch", "sh", "th", not highlighted as correct. A soft aiming reticle rests on central near court, no chosen answer yet. Top-left small HUD title "Rally Pals"; beneath it a small rally counter with tennis-ball symbols, no timer. Top center compact task card shows ONLY an unlabelled fish illustration, speaker icon and an empty final-sound slot. Do not print fish anywhere, even signs. Top-right pause button. Bottom-left a big translucent left/right movement rocker. Bottom-right a generous rounded button labelled "Swing" and a smaller button labelled "Lob". Small replay speaker near task card. The principal visual is a real tennis rally and directional shot play, not answer cards or a menu. Original stylized console graphics, depth, racket/ball/court coherent perspective. No classroom board or word quiz screen.

GAME: BURROW BUILDERS. Wide three-quarter elevated isometric game camera looking across a lush small voxel meadow island. Original chunky cubic terrain, warm sculpted wooden cubes and stone blocks with beveled edges, clean grass steps, winding shallow stream, a bridge partly built across it, a small house under construction with an open door, garden beds and a material-gathering quarry. NO copied Minecraft textures, logos, characters, enemies or trademark art. Bouncy the yellow spring-legged lamb stands by the construction site, carrying one unlabelled wooden cube ready to snap into a glowing wireframe placement preview at the actual house corner. There is a small editable voxel grid and several plainly visible constructed blocks; this is active building, not a pretty landscape backdrop. Top-left small HUD title exactly "Burrow Builders". Top-center compact task card has ONLY an unlabelled picture of a tiny wooden hut, a speaker icon and three empty square answer slots. NO word hut anywhere, no full target spelling. Top-right pause and a small overhead map silhouette. Bottom edge material inventory contains independent chunky cubes labelled with the separate lowercase graphemes exactly "t", "m", "u", "r", "h", "e" in that order, each equally styled, none preselected. Bottom-left directional control; bottom-right two large round buttons labelled "Place" and "Pick up", plus a small camera rotate symbol. Sparse interface, physical block construction obvious, cozy console-game depth and beautiful light. Leave open space in the foreground for play.
